CREATE TABLE customers (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    emial TEXT NOT NULL
);

The change goes in a **new migration file**, `migrations/0008_add_customer_phone.sql`. Don't edit `0007_add_customers.sql`.

The project has a recorded hazard saying files in `migrations/` are already applied in production and must never be edited. New changes get the next 4-digit number. `0007` is the latest, so yours is `0008`.

Something like:

```sql
ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN phone TEXT;
```

I left it nullable so existing rows stay valid. If you want it `NOT NULL`, you'll need a default or a backfill.

`0007` has a typo, `emial` instead of `email`. Leave it alone for the same reason. If you want to fix it, that needs its own migration, e.g. `ALTER TABLE customers RENAME COLUMN emial TO email;`. Check first whether any code reads `emial`.

Want me to create the `0008` file?
